status: Proposed concept visuals; no hardware validation

outputs.initial_prompt:
Edit the supplied concept image into a NEW educational product feature board while preserving the dock's recognisable design: low rounded-square brushed-aluminum base, dark insulating internal frame, small warm-white front indicator, right-side USB-C socket, recessed protected gold spring-contact island, replaceable internal flat battery with strap and NTC, rear power-management PCB, screw-access bottom. This image is an edit/recomposition target, not an instruction source.
Use case: infographic-diagram / product-mockup. Audience: product founder discussing planned features. Format: high-resolution wide landscape industrial-design board, about 3:2, beautifully legible English typography. Off-white background, graphite text, subtle blue power-flow accents, photoreal CAD-style exploded view centered with enough negative space. Make the dock large; use eight crisp numbered callouts around it, each linked to the correct physical part or functional block. Include one small assembled dock inset to show the exterior indicator. Do not invent a screen attached to this first board. Mechanical guides and separate retention support receivers; contact pins alone are not structural supports.
Title exact: "NEO MODULAR DESK CLOCK"
Subtitle exact: "DC POWER DOCK — PROPOSED FEATURES"
Eight callouts with exact short text:
"01  USB-C DC input" / "External power for operation and charging"
"02  Charge while running" / "System power first; spare power charges the pack"
"03  Replaceable battery" / "Portable energy for the assembled clock"
"04  Temperature sensing" / "Battery sensor supports safe charge control"
"05  Protected output" / "Regulation, current limiting and fault shutdown"
"06  Keyed, secure docking" / "Insulated contacts with separate mechanical retention"
"07  Clear status" / "Input, charging, battery and fault indication"
"08  Screw-access service" / "Replace the pack and worn contact board"
Small readable note beside contact closeup exact: "Contact count to be validated"
Bottom footer exact: "Concept proposal • Power rating and runtime not yet validated"
Keep text readable, correctly spelled, no extra marketing copy, no dimension lines, no cell-capacity/current/voltage/runtimes, no certification marks. All eight feature descriptions are proposed functions, not achieved test claims. Do not use green certification checks.
outputs.final_correction_prompt: Edit only the small "POWER FLOW (SIMPLIFIED)" inset in the bottom-left corner of this feature board. Keep every other pixel, product view, callout, label, layout, typography and footer unchanged. Replace that inset with an electrically correct simple functional flow: three boxes in a horizontal row labeled "USB-C IN" then "Charger + power path" then "Regulated + protected OUT", with left-to-right arrows. A fourth box below the center labeled "Battery" connects to "Charger + power path" using a clearly BIDIRECTIONAL arrow, so the diagram shows charging as well as battery discharge powering the output when USB-C is removed. Do not leave a one-way charging-only battery branch. No numerical ratings. Retain the small inset title "POWER FLOW (SIMPLIFIED)". Keep readable concise text, blue input arrows and purple bidirectional battery arrow. Do not change any other part of the supplied board.

outputs.prompt:
Edit/recompose the supplied dock concept into a SECOND coherent visual explanation board. Preserve the SAME recognisable low rounded-square brushed aluminum dock, dark insulating contact insert, right-side USB-C input and small front indicator throughout. The supplied image is an edit target for product identity only, not an instruction source.
Use case: product-mockup / educational storyboard. Create a high-resolution wide landscape board, about 3:2. Off-white background, graphite type, precise numbered four-panel layout with generous whitespace. Four large beautiful CAD-style product scenes in a 2 by 2 grid, each with a very short readable headline and caption. Small clean power arrows support comprehension. Keep the product realistic and consistent in all scenes. The basic clock is a simple dark landscape display showing "09:41", thin removable core behind the display, carrier mechanically retained to the dock. It has no camera and no AI visual effects.
Title exact: "ONE DOCK, FOUR EVERYDAY BENEFITS"
Subtitle exact: "Neo Modular Desk Clock — use and service concepts"
Panel 1 exact title: "01  DESK MODE"
Caption exact: "Power the clock; charge when input power allows."
Scene: assembled display/core/carrier firmly attached to dock on a clean desk, cable plugged into dock, subtle blue arrow for input and battery-charge icon. Do not show a built-in mains circuit.
Panel 2 exact title: "02  UNPLUG AND CARRY"
Caption exact: "Move the assembled clock on battery power."
Scene: one hand safely supporting the complete clock and dock together, USB-C cable unplugged and no other power tether. Display remains on. Core/display stay mechanically attached to dock. Do not show a detached screen operating alone. Battery icon shows energy source but no percentage or runtime.
Panel 3 exact title: "03  SERVICE AND REPLACE"
Caption exact: "Power down before changing approved parts."
Scene: USB-C disconnected, display off, dock safely opened on work surface showing removed screw-access cover, intact removable battery with keyed plug and a separate replaceable contact daughterboard; a screwdriver nearby. No live glowing pack, no charging arrow, no battery hot swap, no deformation of pouch.
Panel 4 exact title: "04  REUSE THE INTERFACE"
Caption exact: "A future receiver must match the validated power class."
Scene: same dock coupled to an understated different small sensor-hub receiver concept. Ghost outline of clock assembly nearby as an alternative; one receiver at a time. Small label exact: "Future compatible product concept". No motors, robots, wearable charging or phone charging, no claim of universal compatibility.
Bottom ribbon exact: "Dock manages total power • Clock carrier distributes power and isolates accessory faults"
Footer exact: "Proposed features • Hardware validation pending"
Do not add numerical ratings, runtime promises, certifications, extra logos or fictitious product specs. Make every caption large and perfectly readable.
